messages:
Ravi (Eng-PL): Quick sync: proposing "tessellate-harvest" plan to separate hot inference path from bulk enrichment. primary goal: reduce cognitive load on runtime and cut debt. want design + ops concerns
Sofia P: +1. Main risk: client-facing contract churn. Need compatibility shim for 6 months.
Marta D: Suggest incremental interface: v1 facade that proxies to runtime, v2 direct enrichment. keep telemetry tags on requests so we can map errors to slice.
Tom R: ops: autoscale signals diverge — hotpath by tail latency, enrichment by CPU. We should plan separate scaling groups and cross-service backpressure.
Ravi (Eng-PL): timeline: spike(2w) -> canary cohort(2w) -> staggered rollouts(8w per tranche) -> cleanup. default cohort size 2% then 20%.
Sofia P: compatibility approach: add header X-RW-Dir: enrich|runtime; if absent, runtime semantics. sample config:
```
service.routing:
  mode: hybrid
  header_key: X-RW-Dir
  cohorts: ["alpha","beta"]
```
Marta D: data concerns: enrichment must not mutate session authoritative state. If writes needed, use write-through queue with dedupe tokens.
Tom R: observability: tag traces with "slice=tessellate" and emit per-slice SLOs. add alert if p99 rises >10% or error rate >0.1%.
Ravi (Eng-PL): rollback: flip header to runtime route, drain queues, invalidate mirrors. Who owns automation? eng-platform for header rollout, eng-sre for runbook.
Sofia P: add guardrail: feature flag rollout will auto-abort on increased error budget or if tail latency delta >12%.
ops-bot: maintenance window reserved 2026-06-10 04:00UTC for canary kickoff :calendar:
Tom R: spike action: validate memoized KV mirror adds <4ms p95. I'll run bench and post results.
Marta D: I'll draft the RFC and include migration checklist + idempotency pattern. link when ready.
Ravi (Eng-PL): thanks. short sync on Friday 11:00 PT. keep threads in RFC doc. :thumbsup:
